metadata.description: Curated evaluation set for LegalAI retrieval and citation accuracy measurement

eval_set.question: What is BNS Section 316 and how does it replace IPC 420?
eval_set.ground_truth: BNS Section 316 corresponds to IPC Section 420 which deals with cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property. The punishment is imprisonment up to 7 years and fine.

eval_set.question: What are the legal steps to file an FIR for cybercrime?
eval_set.ground_truth: File FIR at local police station or cybercrime cell. Cognizable offences under IT Act Section 66 and BNS. Provide evidence: screenshots, transaction records.

eval_set.question: What is the punishment for murder under BNS 2023?
eval_set.ground_truth: BNS Section 101 (replacing IPC 302) prescribes death or life imprisonment for murder, plus fine. Death only in rarest of rare cases per Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab.

eval_set.question: How to apply for anticipatory bail under BNSS 2023?
eval_set.ground_truth: File application in Sessions Court or High Court under BNSS Section 482 (formerly CrPC 438) apprehending arrest. Court considers nature of accusation, antecedents, possibility of fleeing.

eval_set.question: What rights do I have when police arrest me without a warrant?
eval_set.ground_truth: Article 22 guarantees right to know grounds of arrest, right to legal representation, and production before magistrate within 24 hours. BNSS Section 47 governs arrest procedure.

eval_set.question: What is the punishment for domestic violence and dowry harassment?
eval_set.ground_truth: BNS Section 85 (IPC 498A) punishes husband/relatives for cruelty with imprisonment up to 3 years and fine. Domestic Violence Act 2005 provides civil remedies including protection orders.

eval_set.question: What is Article 21 and what rights does it protect?
eval_set.ground_truth: Article 21: No person shall be deprived of life or personal liberty except by procedure established by law. Expanded to include right to dignity, livelihood, health, education per Maneka Gandhi v. UoI.

eval_set.question: What are Fundamental Rights under the Indian Constitution?
eval_set.ground_truth: Fundamental Rights (Articles 12-35): Right to Equality (14-18), Right to Freedom (19-22), Right against Exploitation (23-24), Right to Religion (25-28), Cultural rights (29-30), Right to Constitutional Remedies (32).

eval_set.question: How to file a writ petition in High Court?
eval_set.ground_truth: File writ petition under Article 226 in High Court or Article 32 in Supreme Court. Types: Habeas Corpus (illegal detention), Mandamus (public duty), Certiorari (quash orders), Prohibition, Quo Warranto.

eval_set.question: How to file a consumer complaint against Amazon for defective product?
eval_set.ground_truth: File complaint in District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (up to Rs 1 crore claims) under Consumer Protection Act 2019. Provide purchase proof, defect evidence, and prior complaint to seller.

eval_set.question: What is the time limit to file a consumer complaint?
eval_set.ground_truth: Under Section 69, complaint must be filed within 2 years from cause of action. Commission can condone delay if sufficient cause is shown.

eval_set.question: What compensation can I get in a consumer case?
eval_set.ground_truth: District/State/National Commission can order: refund, repair/replacement, compensation for loss/injury, punitive damages for reckless disregard, and litigation costs.

eval_set.question: What are the grounds for divorce under Hindu Marriage Act?
eval_set.ground_truth: Hindu Marriage Act Section 13 grounds: adultery, cruelty, desertion (2+ years), conversion, mental disorder, leprosy, venereal disease, renunciation, presumption of death. Mutual consent under 13B.

eval_set.question: How is child custody decided after divorce?
eval_set.ground_truth: Courts consider welfare/best interest of child as paramount. Mother generally gets custody of children under 5. Father has natural guardianship. Courts may grant joint custody.

eval_set.question: What is the legal process for maintenance after separation?
eval_set.ground_truth: BNSS Section 144 (formerly CrPC 125): Magistrate can order maintenance for wife, children, parents who cannot maintain themselves. Court considers income, needs, and lifestyle standard.

eval_set.question: What legal action can I take if my landlord is illegally evicting me?
eval_set.ground_truth: Landlord must follow due process: valid eviction notice, valid legal grounds (non-payment, personal need). File injunction in civil court. State Rent Control Acts provide additional protection.

eval_set.question: How to register a property sale agreement?
eval_set.ground_truth: Property sale above Rs 100 must be registered under Registration Act. Execute sale deed, pay stamp duty (state-specific), register at Sub-Registrar's office with witnesses and ID proof.

eval_set.question: What is the law for online fraud in India?
eval_set.ground_truth: IT Act Section 66D: cheating by personation using computer/internet, punishable up to 3 years and Rs 1 lakh fine. BNS 318 (IPC 420) also applies. Report to cybercrime.gov.in.

eval_set.question: What to do if someone is blackmailing me online?
eval_set.ground_truth: IT Act 67A (obscene material), BNS 351 (criminal intimidation). Preserve evidence: screenshots. Report to cybercrime.gov.in or nearest police station. Do not pay the extortionist.

eval_set.question: What can I do if my employer is not paying salary?
eval_set.ground_truth: File complaint with Payment of Wages Authority or Labour Commissioner. Can also approach Labour Court under Industrial Disputes Act. File complaint within 1 year of due date.

eval_set.question: What is the procedure for wrongful termination claim?
eval_set.ground_truth: Termination without notice or compensation for 1+ year employees violates ID Act Section 25F. File complaint with Labour Court for reinstatement or compensation. Notice: 1 month or pay in lieu.

eval_set.question: What is the difference between bailable and non-bailable offences?
eval_set.ground_truth: Bailable offences: bail is a right, police officer can grant bail. Non-bailable: bail at court's discretion, consider gravity, criminal antecedents, flight risk. First Schedule BNSS lists classification.

eval_set.question: What is Right to Information (RTI) and how to file an RTI application?
eval_set.ground_truth: RTI Act 2005: Citizen can request information from Public Authorities. File application to Public Information Officer with Rs 10 fee. Response within 30 days. Appeal to First Appellate Authority then CIC/SIC.

eval_set.question: What are the rights of an accused person in India?
eval_set.ground_truth: Constitutional rights: protection against self-incrimination (Art 20), right to life/liberty (Art 21), rights on arrest (Art 22). Right to free legal aid, speedy trial, know charges, bail hearing.

eval_set.question: What is the difference between District, State, and National Consumer Commissions?
eval_set.ground_truth: District Commission: up to Rs 1 crore. State Commission: Rs 1 crore to Rs 10 crore. NCDRC (National): above Rs 10 crore. Complaints filed based on claim value.

eval_set.question: What is Lok Adalat and how does it help in dispute resolution?
eval_set.ground_truth: Lok Adalat: alternative dispute resolution forum under Legal Services Authorities Act. Awards are final (no appeal), cases settled amicably. No court fees. Covers motor accident, matrimonial, labour disputes.

eval_set.question: What is the POCSO Act and what protection does it provide to children?
eval_set.ground_truth: POCSO Act 2012 protects children under 18 from sexual offences. Mandatory reporting by all (Section 19). Special courts for trial. Penetrative assault: minimum 10 years (Sec 4). Aggravated: minimum 20 years (Sec 6).

eval_set.question: What are the PF and gratuity rights of an employee?
eval_set.ground_truth: EPF: 12% employee + 12% employer contribution mandatory for establishments with 20+ employees. Gratuity: 15 days salary per year after 5 years service under Payment of Gratuity Act.

eval_set.question: What is the law regarding data privacy in India?
eval_set.ground_truth: Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 governs data privacy. IT Act 43A: body corporates must maintain reasonable security for sensitive personal data. Penalties for breaches.

eval_set.question: What is the Benami Transactions Act and how does it affect property ownership?
eval_set.ground_truth: Benami Transactions (Prohibition) Act 1988: property held in another's name but financed by someone else is benami. Punishable with 7 years imprisonment. Property can be confiscated by government.

eval_set.question: What is cognizable and non-cognizable offence?
eval_set.ground_truth: Cognizable offence: police can arrest without warrant (murder, rape, robbery). Non-cognizable: police need magistrate's order to investigate (assault, fraud). First Schedule of BNSS lists classification.

eval_set.question: What are the legal rights of a woman in a live-in relationship?
eval_set.ground_truth: Supreme Court has held live-in relationships akin to marriage under Domestic Violence Act. Women can claim maintenance and protection orders. Children born are legitimate. No specific law for live-in marriage rights.

eval_set.question: What is the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act?
eval_set.ground_truth: Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Act 2013: Employers with 10+ employees must form Internal Complaints Committee. Complaints investigated within 90 days. Penalties for employer non-compliance.

eval_set.question: What is the process of filing a private complaint in Magistrate's court?
eval_set.ground_truth: File complaint before Judicial Magistrate under BNSS Section 223. Magistrate examines complainant and witnesses on oath. If satisfied, can take cognizance and issue summons/warrant.

eval_set.question: Can I file a consumer complaint against a hospital for medical negligence?
eval_set.ground_truth: Medical services are 'services' under Consumer Protection Act. Patients can file complaints for medical negligence (deficiency in service) before District/State/National Commission and seek compensation.

eval_set.question: What is the process to get free legal aid in India?
eval_set.ground_truth: Free legal aid under Legal Services Authorities Act: available to women, SC/ST, persons with disability, those earning under Rs 1 lakh/year. Contact NALSA (15100) or District Legal Services Authority.

eval_set.question: What is the zero FIR and how is it different from a regular FIR?
eval_set.ground_truth: Zero FIR: registered at any police station regardless of jurisdiction. Regular FIR: must be filed in jurisdictional police station. BNSS Section 173 mandates registration. Zero FIR transferred to appropriate station.

eval_set.question: What is the punishment for hacking under IT Act?
eval_set.ground_truth: IT Act Section 66: unauthorized access to computer/network, imprisonment up to 3 years or fine up to Rs 5 lakh, or both. Section 43: civil liability for damage to computer, compensation up to Rs 1 crore.

eval_set.question: What is adverse possession and can I claim ownership of land I have occupied for years?
eval_set.ground_truth: Adverse possession: continuous, open, hostile occupation for 12 years can give title under Limitation Act Section 65. Must file declaratory suit to get legal title recognized by court.

eval_set.question: What is a power of attorney and how to create one?
eval_set.ground_truth: Power of Attorney authorizes agent to act on principal's behalf. General POA: multiple acts. Special POA: specific transaction. Execute on stamp paper, notarize. Registration required for immovable property transactions.

eval_set.question: What is sedition law in India and what replaced it?
eval_set.ground_truth: IPC Section 124A (sedition) has been replaced by BNS Section 152 which penalizes acts endangering sovereignty, unity and integrity of India. Punishment: life imprisonment to 7 years and fine.

eval_set.question: What is the scope of freedom of speech under Article 19?
eval_set.ground_truth: Article 19(1)(a): right to freedom of speech and expression. Subject to reasonable restrictions under 19(2): sovereignty, integrity, security, friendly relations with foreign states, public order, decency, contempt of court, defamation.

eval_set.question: What is the Maternity Benefit Act and how many weeks of leave am I entitled to?
eval_set.ground_truth: Maternity Benefit Act 1961 (amended 2017): 26 weeks paid maternity leave for first two children, 12 weeks for subsequent. Adoption/commissioning mothers: 12 weeks. Establishments with 50+ employees must provide creche.

eval_set.question: What is an unfair trade practice under Consumer Protection Act?
eval_set.ground_truth: Consumer Protection Act defines unfair trade practices: false representations about goods/services, misleading advertisements, offering gifts with hidden conditions, hoarding, and deceptive pricing practices.

eval_set.question: What is the inheritance right of a daughter under Hindu law?
eval_set.ground_truth: Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act 2005: daughters have equal coparcenary rights as sons in ancestral property. Supreme Court in Vineeta Sharma (2020) held this applies even if father died before 2005.

eval_set.question: What is plea bargaining and when can it be used?
eval_set.ground_truth: BNSS Chapter XXVII (CrPC Chapter XXIA): plea bargaining for offences with punishment up to 7 years (not socio-economic offences or against women/children). Accused pleads guilty, court gives reduced sentence.

eval_set.question: What is RERA and how does it protect home buyers?
eval_set.ground_truth: Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act 2016: Builders must register projects with RERA. Mandatory disclosure of project details. Buyers entitled to compensation for delay in possession. File complaints with RERA authority.

eval_set.question: What is the law on cyberbullying and online harassment in India?
eval_set.ground_truth: BNS Section 79 (cyberstalking), Section 351 (criminal intimidation). IT Act Section 66A (partly struck down by SC). File FIR at cybercrime cell or cybercrime.gov.in. Gather evidence: screenshots, timestamps.

eval_set.question: What is the National Green Tribunal and what cases can it hear?
eval_set.ground_truth: National Green Tribunal Act 2010: NGT hears substantial questions relating to environment, forests, wildlife, biodiversity, water, air, pollution cases. Can award compensation and restoration orders. Appeals to Supreme Court.

eval_set.question: What is the difference between IPC and BNS 2023?
eval_set.ground_truth: BNS (Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita) 2023 replaced IPC 1860. Key changes: sections renumbered, organized crime added (BNS 111), terrorism defined, sedition replaced with BNS 152, death penalty for mob lynching. More comprehensive.
